**Ordering rule.** For every valid work pick, I save the record first: `work_started: true`, the course or one-shot action, accounting, deletion of `/tmp/gatekeep-note.synthetic`, and `reject: null`. Only then does the handler make its first dispatch or external write. Picks that are not work picks never touch `work_started` or `reject_withdrawn`.

## Pick boundary

| Pick | work_started | course | reject_withdrawn | Other record effects at the boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: deliver (row 2) | false -> true | null -> deliver | false | Note deleted, reject null; caps stay 10/10, usage 0/0 |
| B: assess (row 3) | false -> true | null -> assess | false | Note deleted, reject null |
| C: deliver (row 2) | false -> true | null -> deliver | false | Note deleted, reject null; caps 10/10 |
| E: deliver (earlier pick) | already true | deliver | false | Unchanged by the external head move |
| D: back (row 5, sole pick) | stays false | stays null | false -> true | Reject-menu post_steps dropped, note deleted, reject null; blockers unchanged |
| deliver with nits | -> true | -> deliver-nits | unchanged | Note deleted, reject null |
| fix nits, course null | -> true | stays null | unchanged | `repair.wave.action: fix-nits`; selected ids and payloads saved; missing accounting initialized; no standing course |
| approve workflow run | -> true | unchanged | unchanged | Its permission check still applies inside the handler |
| approve | -> true | unchanged | unchanged | approved_head is written only after success |
| merge | -> true | unchanged | unchanged | Merge preconditions and compare-and-swap still apply inside the handler |
| assess, zero blockers | -> true | -> assess | unchanged | Posts nothing; GitHub baseline unchanged |
| show evidence | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | Prints the record, then re-renders the same menu |
| check test flaky | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | No disposition is recorded here, and the name grants nothing |
| overrule 1 | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | Not executed in this probe |
| invalid input | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | Clarifying question, nothing runs |
| a reject-menu step | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged | Settles only through reject.md |

## A - deliver, then needs input

**Narration**
- The repair returns `open - needs source fixture`.
- No round is charged: there was a needs decision and no source change. Usage stays 0/0.
- Exit check records the needs result in `repair.wave.no_progress` and exits `stuck - needs source fixture`.
- No review, push or watch runs.

**Report**

This PR adds an indexing job to example/widgets. There is no spec, so it is judged on the PR's promise to index the catalog, and you are the author.

One problem blocks merging, and the repair could not fix it.

Problem 1

### What is blocked
The PR's indexing job keeps its own copy of the catalog, but the architecture document says the catalog lives in one place (docs/architecture.md:12).

### Why the repair stopped
The repair tried to remove that copy and read the existing stream of catalog edits, the change feed, instead. It came back without a change because it needs a source fixture that the repository does not have.

### What you can do
- stop: end this run and leave the PR as it is.
- deliver: try the repair again with 10 more repair and sync attempts. It stops again unless the source fixture becomes available.
- assess: post this problem to the PR as a review comment and make no repairs.
- overrule 1: set this problem aside for this run.

## C - deliver, repaired

**Narration**
1. The finding artifacts are written. On pi, one `loop-implementer` row runs with cwd /work/widgets-pr-88. On Claude Code, one native implementer helper runs instead. In both cases the finding to close is P1's `instead:` remedy, carrying `builds:`, docs/architecture.md:12, and test/index.test.js.
2. The commit is admitted, and the round counts once: 1 of 10.
3. A fresh pre-push reviewer gets these closure inputs and scope:
   - Re-review task with P1's `builds:`, `instead:` and evidence as the previous report.
   - `## Fix delta` = `git diff aaaa… HEAD`.
   - It reviews code only inside that delta and gives P1 a closure line.
   - It repeats no whole-PR approach judgment.
4. The reviewer reports `P1: resolved` and no new findings.
5. One push lands, to bbbb…. The pre-menu refresh and comment reconciliation find no delta.
6. No claim recheck runs, because the claims carry to the pushed commit. All merge preconditions pass.

**Report**

Nothing blocks merging. The repair replaced the separate catalog copy with the existing change feed, the reviewer confirmed the fix, and required checks passed on the pushed commit.

**Narration**
1. The head moved without an own push, so the run re-enters step 3:
   - Prior-review selection is refreshed and returns null.
   - Scope is re-selected: PR intent.
   - Verify runs at cccc… with green evidence.
2. Step 4 runs on both harnesses (pi `wave-reviewer`, or the Claude Code native reviewer, cwd /work/widgets-pr-88) with these inputs:
   - Re-review task carrying P1's `builds:`, `instead:` and evidence under its contributor IDs.
   - The task requires a resolved or open closure line for P1.
   - No whole-PR approach input, no `## Approach conflicts` appendix, and no new conflicts.
   - Native code review covers the whole `origin/main...cccc…` diff, because the prior review is null.
3. The native report has no new findings and `P1: resolved`, so P1 closes and its ID stays in the ledger.
4. Readiness exit applies. Usage stays 0/0.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Each checkpoint is independent. For a valid work pick, save `work_started: true`, remove the saved rejection note, and persist the selected course before the handler's first dispatch or external write. No tracker is reinitialized, and no tools run in this exercise.

| Pick or checkpoint | Saved progress at the boundary and supplied continuation |
|---|---|
| A: deliver | Set `work_started: true`, course `deliver`, and clear the saved note. Retain the returned need for a source fixture and the unchanged prerequisite; record no completed repair. |
| B: assess | Set `work_started: true`, course `assess`, and clear the saved note. Record the successful head-pinned COMMENT review and confirmed commit; keep the approach problem open. |
| C: deliver | Set `work_started: true`, course `deliver`, and clear the saved note. Record the reviewer's resolved closure, successful push, and fresh evidence at `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. |
| E: existing deliver | Keep `work_started: true` and course `deliver`; rejection remains unavailable. Bind fresh evidence and the resolved closure to `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`. |
| D: reject, then back | Reject entry leaves `work_started: false` and course null. Back saves `reject_withdrawn: true`, clears reject-menu steps, deletes the note, and sets `reject: null`; it changes no blocker. |
| deliver with nits | Set `work_started: true`, course `deliver-nits`. |
| fix nits, course null | Set `work_started: true`; keep course null and save the one-iteration selection before its handler. |
| approve workflow run; approve; merge | Set `work_started: true`; leave course unchanged. Each handler retains its separate permission and freshness checks. |
| assess with zero blockers | Set `work_started: true`, course `assess`, even though its handler posts nothing. |
| show evidence; check test flaky; overrule 1; invalid input | Leave `work_started` and course unchanged at this boundary. This classification executes no inspection, disposition, or overrule. |
| reject-menu step | Leave `work_started` and course unchanged. The retained mapping, selected step, permissions, and freshness guards—not the fixture's labels—determine any later authority. |

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved five facts from fails to holds and kept the one Before already held. The explicit ordering rule (save work_started true, delete the note and set reject null before the first dispatch or external write) fixed boundary, where Before saved the flag but never cleared the note. Classifying zero-blocker assess as a work pick fixed other-picks, where Before left work_started false. In C, naming P1's `instead:` remedy with `builds:`, docs/architecture.md:12 and test/index.test.js as the finding to close, plus a delta-only pre-push review that requires a closure line and repeats no whole-PR approach judgment, fixed closure; Before sent only finding text, evidence and the test. In E, carrying P1's builds/instead/evidence under contributor IDs to step 4 despite the null prior review, requiring a closure line and barring new conflicts, fixed external; Before attached no previous report and reviewed the whole diff fresh. In D, persisting reject_withdrawn true, deleting the note, setting reject null and stating nothing was posted or closed fixed back; Before wrote nothing. Continuation held in both: the obstacle names the missing fixture with stop recommended, assess-terminal recommends stop with no merge or approve, and neither resets the flag, course or usage. To keep these, retain the single save-before-work sentence. Three spots are thinner than the facts they support: say outright that work_started stays true through the A and B re-entries rather than leaving it to the table; in C, say that the resolved P1 line is carried to the exact pushed head with no second whole-wave review; and in E, word the whole-diff native code review so it cannot be read as a renewed approach judgment. The new `overrule <n>` hint and the A 'What you can do' bullet are harmless to these facts as long as overrule never appears as a numbered row and reject never returns.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved four facts and lost none. Boundary moved because the table now clears the saved rejection note alongside work_started and the course before the first dispatch or external write; Before only saved the flag and course. Closure moved because C now names the change-feed replacement as the remedy to close, together with the original mechanism, base evidence and test/index.test.js, and rules out a repeated approach judgment after the push; Before listed builds, base evidence and the test but never the replacement remedy. External moved because E now treats the carried problem as closure-only under its existing ID with no new conflict, where Before re-reviewed the mechanism approach across the whole diff. Back moved because D now saves reject_withdrawn true, deletes the note, sets reject null and says nothing was posted or closed, where Before refused to change reject_withdrawn. Other-picks and continuation held in both. Three places are thin and worth firming up: D never says the refresh ran and returned the unchanged head, A and B only imply that work_started stays true after the failed repair and after assess, and E asks for a 'resolved/open line' without calling it the minted contributor closure line. Keep the overrule hint and the three-section stuck-blocker block clear of any reject row or note preview in post-work menus, and keep the wording that fix nits leaves course null.
